subject: Pilot economics + model mix — follow-up, budget bands & next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Wong <claire@brightworks.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot economics + model mix — follow-up, budget bands & next steps

Claire — thanks for the time today. Quick write-up of what we discussed so we have alignment before I send the token workbook and SOW draft. TL;DR: target pilot budget band and per-model mix will determine whether we lean heavier on quantized chat models + cached embeddings or a higher-fidelity chat variant.

Notes from the call:
- Expected steady-state volume (your estimate): 20–35M user prompt tokens/day (ballpark) — ~600M–1.05B tokens/month. You confirmed 70% of calls will be short chat queries, 25% embeddings (search/semantic match), 5% higher-cost rerank calls.
- Proposed model mix for pricing exercise: chat (streaming) = 65%, embeddings = 30%, rerank = 5%. If you see heavy embedding reuse we can shift cache/batch strategy.
- Unit economics target you mentioned: ~ $700–$1,200 per 1M tokens as the acceptable blended price for the pilot (you were hoping to land closer to the low end).

What I’m sending with this email:
- BrightWorks_token_estimates.xlsx (workbook): line-item token forecast by endpoint, blended $/1M scenarios (conservative / baseline / aggressive).
- BW_SOW_draft_v1.pdf: short pilot SOW (2 weeks sandbox + 4-week pilot, success criteria, data / IP notes, SLAs).

Recommended next steps (simple):
1) You and Tom review the attached workbook and mark the realistic monthly token band (low/expected/high).
2) We run a short unit-econ simulation (we’ll return a blended $/1M token figure under each mix and latency/SLO assumptions).
3) If the numbers look OK, we finalize SOW and target a pilot start in ~2 weeks.

Open questions for your team (please reply inline):
- Do you expect the embeddings usage to be mostly writes (new vectors) or reads (search rerank + frequent similarity queries)? That affects cache effectiveness.
- Rerank calls: are they full text-level scoring (expensive) or a small candidate rerank (cheaper)?

If helpful I can run two quick scenarios and call back with one-pager: (A) 600M/mo tokens @ our recommended model mix, and (B) 1B/mo tokens with adjusted batching/quantization.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Wong <claire@brightworks.com>

Cc: Tom Miller <tom.miller@brightworks.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot economics + model mix — follow-up, budget bands & next steps

Neha — appreciate the recap and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 20–35M/day number is what product estimates said for Q1 scaled usage; for an initial pilot we expect ~15–25% of that (so ~150–260M/mo), but we want to test at the higher band to validate caching and rerank assumptions.
- Embeddings will be read-heavy (search + freshness window ~24 hours) — we’ll do periodic bulk upserts but mostly queries.
- Rerank is small-candidate scoring (top 50) rather than full-document attention, so cost per rerank should be closer to mid-tier.

Budget band: we can reasonably commit $12k–$35k/month for pilot spend depending on results and unit-econ. Our finance lead (copied) prefers an initial cap; can you show blended $/1M token scenarios that land at ~$700 and ~$1,100 so we can see trade-offs?

Also would like an example latency/SLA box (p90 target, throughput) you’d include in the SOW.

Thanks — I’ll review attachments and sync with procurement.

—Claire
Claire Wong
Head of Product, BrightWorks
claire@brightworks.com

Looping infra and pricing — I drafted two quick blended scenarios and updated the workbook (see attached). Key assumptions I used:
- Scenario A (conservative): 200M tokens/mo, mix chat 60% / embed 35% / rerank 5%, blended $/1M = $980.
- Scenario B (aggressive): 800M tokens/mo, mix chat 68% / embed 28% / rerank 4%, blended $/1M = $640 (uses aggressive batching + quantized chat model).

Rishi — can you sanity-check the batching assumptions (latency vs batch size) and call out any fallback model we should propose if the customer needs tighter latency? I put draft notes in the second tab of the workbook.
